content.title: Recommendations for management of patients with HF and AF (excerpt)
content.summary: Guideline recommendations covering anticoagulation, rate control, rhythm interventions, revascularization, and use of SGLT2 inhibitors in patients with heart failure (HF) and atrial fibrillation (AF), with a short abbreviation list.

recommendations.detail: DOACs are recommended in preference to VKAs in patients with HF, except in those with moderate or severe mitral stenosis or mechanical prosthetic heart valves. For patients with HF and non-valvular AF eligible for anticoagulation based on a CHA2DS2-VASc score, NOACs rather than warfarin should be considered for anticoagulation as NOACs are associated with a lower risk of stroke, intracranial haemorrhage, and mortality.

Beta-blockers should be considered for short- and long-term rate control in patients with HF and AF. For patients in NYHA class I–III, a beta-blocker is usually given orally and is recommended as first-line treatment to control ventricular rate, provided the patient is euvolaemic.

In cases of a clear association between paroxysmal or persistent AF and worsening of HF symptoms despite medical therapy, catheter ablation should be considered for the prevention of AF. AV node catheter ablation may be considered to control heart rate and relieve symptoms in patients unresponsive to or intolerant of pharmacological rate and rhythm control therapy.

Coronary revascularization should be considered to relieve persistent symptoms of angina in patients with HFrEF/CCS and coronary anatomy suitable for revascularization, despite optimal medical therapy (including anti-anginal drugs). Myocardial revascularization is recommended when angina persists despite treatment.

SGLT2 inhibitors (canagliflozin, dapagliflozin, empagliflozin, ertugliflozin, sotagliflozin) are recommended in patients with T2DM at risk of CV events to reduce hospitalizations for heart failure, major cardiovascular events, end-stage renal dysfunction, and CV death. Empagliflozin specifically is mentioned as a consideration in patients with T2DM to prevent or delay onset of HF and prolong life.

abbreviations.CHA2DS2-VASc: congestive heart failure or left ventricular dysfunction, Hypertension, Age ≥75 (doubled), Diabetes, Stroke (doubled) - Vascular disease, Age 65–74, Sex category (female) (score)
abbreviations.HFrEF: heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
abbreviations.QRS: Q, R, and S waves of an ECG
